featuredImage.alt: What to Do With Old Appliances

c: Getting rid of an old appliance isn’t always as simple as putting it at the curb.
Maybe the refrigerator no longer works. Perhaps the washing machine is too old to sell. Your stove may be damaged, or that old freezer has been sitting in the garage for years.
When an appliance has
, you still have several options.
The important thing is to avoid leaving large appliances sitting around indefinitely or disposing of them incorrectly.

At Live Junk Free, we help homeowners, landlords, property managers, and businesses across the GTA remove unwanted appliances and handle them through responsible disposal, recycling, and donation channels.
Here’s what you can do with appliances that nobody wants to buy or take.

blocks.text: 1. Check Whether Your Municipality Accepts It

c: Before paying for removal, check whether your local municipality offers large-item or appliance collection.
Some municipalities provide scheduled pickup programs for certain appliances.
For Toronto residents, large-item collection may be available for eligible appliances, depending on the municipality’s current rules and pickup requirements.
The downside is that municipal collection may require you to:

items: Move the appliance to an approved location

Ask the retailer whether they offer old-appliance haul-away when delivering the new one.
Some retailers provide removal as part of the delivery service or offer it as an additional option.

blocks.text: 5. Don’t Leave It Sitting in the Garage

c: An old appliance can quickly become permanent storage.
You might tell yourself:

b: “I’ll figure out what to do with it later.”

c: Then months pass.
The appliance continues taking up valuable space.
A large refrigerator, freezer, washer, or dryer can occupy a significant portion of a garage or basement.
If you already know you won’t use it again, arranging removal can help you reclaim that space.

blocks.text: 6. Don’t Try to Move Heavy Appliances Alone

c: This is especially important for refrigerators, washers, dryers, and other large appliances.
They can be:
Trying to move one without the right equipment can result in an injury or damage to your floors, walls, cabinets, or doors.
Professional appliance removal teams have the equipment and experience needed to handle heavy units.
Live Junk Free specifically emphasizes protecting floors, walls, doorways, and surrounding areas during appliance removal.

blocks.text: 7. Be Careful With Refrigerators and Freezers

c: Refrigerators and freezers require extra attention because they can contain refrigerants and other components that shouldn’t simply be released or handled improperly.
If your refrigerator is broken and you want it gone, don’t attempt to dismantle its cooling system yourself.
Instead, use an appropriate municipal program, retailer haul-away service, or professional removal company that knows how to handle the appliance properly.
Live Junk Free states that its appliance disposal process includes appropriate handling of refrigerants and other regulated substances.

blocks.text: 9. Consider the Appliance’s Condition

c: Not every unwanted appliance should automatically go to disposal.
Ask:

b: Does it still work but have cosmetic damage?

c: If it still works, donation or reuse may be possible.
If it’s broken beyond practical repair, recycling or professional disposal may be more appropriate.
The goal is to choose the option that keeps the appliance useful for as long as possible.

blocks.text: 10. Remove the Appliance Before a Renovation

c: If you’re renovating a kitchen or laundry room, old appliances can quickly get in the way.
Removing them before the renovation starts can give contractors more working space.
This is particularly useful when replacing several appliances at once.

c: If you have more than one unwanted appliance, consider removing them together.
Combining items into one service can be more convenient than arranging multiple separate pickups.

blocks.text: 14. Prepare the Appliance for Removal

c: You don’t need to dismantle the appliance yourself.
However, you can make the appointment easier by:

items: Removing food from refrigerators and freezers
Moving small objects away from the appliance

Don’t attempt complicated electrical, gas, or refrigerant work yourself.

blocks.text: 15. What About Appliances That Are Too Old to Recycle?

c: Even very old appliances can contain recyclable materials.
Age doesn’t automatically mean the appliance belongs in a landfill.
Professional recycling facilities can often recover materials from old machines.

blocks.text: What Is the Best Option for an Appliance You Can’t Sell or Donate?

c: The right choice depends on your situation.
Option — Best For — Possible Drawback

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions

items.title: What should I do with an appliance I can’t sell?
text: If an appliance can’t be sold or donated, consider municipal collection, retailer haul-away, appliance recycling, or professional appliance removal.

items.title: Can old appliances be recycled?
text: Yes. Many appliances contain recyclable metals, plastics, electronics, and other recoverable materials. Professional recycling facilities can process these materials appropriately.

items.title: Can I put an old refrigerator in the garbage?
text: Don’t assume that regular garbage collection will accept it. Check your municipality’s large-item collection rules or arrange an appropriate appliance removal service.

items.title: Should I dismantle my old appliance before removal?
text: Usually, you shouldn’t need to. Professional removal companies can handle the heavy lifting and dismantling required for many appliances.

items.title: Can junk removal companies remove refrigerators?
text: Yes. Many professional junk removal companies offer refrigerator and freezer removal. Live Junk Free provides fridge and freezer removal across the GTA.

items.title: Can old washers and dryers be recycled?
text: Yes. Washers and dryers contain substantial amounts of metal and other materials that can be recovered through appropriate recycling processes. Live Junk Free provides washer and dryer removal with environmentally responsible recycling.

items.title: What is the easiest way to get rid of an old appliance?
text: If you don’t want to move the appliance yourself or arrange transportation and disposal, professional appliance removal is often the simplest option.
